pages.title: The briefing
pages.content:
THE HOUR how it runs

THE
HOUR

how it runs

Sixty minutes
in three parts

Our sixty-minute employer briefing provides independent guidance before you select or re-tender a workplace pension scheme. We examine your plan structure alongside up to four of your key organisational leaders.

0–20 min

How is your workplace pension plan assembled in the first twenty minutes?

The opening twenty minutes focus entirely on how your workplace pension plan is constructed. We examine your contribution structures, assessing the required employer and employee contribution levels alongside qualifying earnings calculations. Together, we look at the mechanics of default investment funds, charges, and governance arrangements without promotional sales pitches. Our adviser draws out your contribution curves on a whiteboard, illustrating how differing salary bands and contribution rates affect total organisational outlays over time. These curves serve as clear illustrations rather than speculative projections, allowing your leadership team to understand the true structural foundations of potential schemes before entering discussions with commercial providers or signing binding agreements.

20–40 min

What will your staff be told during the middle twenty minutes?

The second twenty-minute segment addresses employee communication and member experience. We review statutory communications, auto-enrolment notices, and opt-out rules, highlighting how pension concepts can be conveyed clearly without corporate jargon or unnecessary anxiety. An effective scheme requires staff to understand what is deducted from their pay, what the employer contributes on their behalf, and how default funds operate. We help you draft plain-language member letters and outline practical educational formats, such as structured group question-and-answer sessions. Clear communication ensures that your workforce appreciates the pension benefit from day one, reducing administrative enquiries and unnecessary opt-outs across your teams.

40–60 min

How do we establish your one next conversation in the final twenty minutes?

The concluding twenty minutes translate analysis into decisive action by defining your one next conversation. Rather than leaving you with an overwhelming list of tasks, we pinpoint the exact discussion your organisation must have next, whether that involves negotiating terms with existing pension providers, presenting options to your board, or gathering workforce payroll data. We provide twelve specific questions to ask prospective providers so you can evaluate master trusts or commercial offerings on equal footing. Following the session, we prepare a concise written summary and contribution-curve sheet within five working days, giving your management team a permanent, objective record to guide upcoming decisions.

Who should attend the sixty-minute briefing?

We welcome up to four decision-makers from your organisation to participate in the briefing. Typical attendees include your finance lead, human resources manager, a managing director, and an employee representative. Having both financial and people leaders present ensures that structural costs, operational payroll requirements, and staff communications are evaluated collectively. The session can be conducted online via video conference or in person at your office if your premises are located within forty kilometres of our Bristol office. This small group format encourages direct dialogue, allowing all participants to ask pressing questions and reach shared internal clarity within a single focused hour.

What materials should your team prepare in advance?

Preparation is kept intentionally straightforward so you can focus on discussion. Exactly three days before your scheduled appointment, we email you a concise ten-question pre-briefing form. This form gathers basic organisational details: your total staff headcount, your current workplace pension arrangement if one exists, existing contribution rates, payroll frequency, and whether you operate across multiple sites or languages. Having this background beforehand allows our independent adviser to prepare tailored contribution curves in advance. You do not need to assemble extensive actuarial paperwork or legal files; completing our ten basic questions ensures the sixty-minute briefing addresses your specific organisational realities immediately.

Staff headcount

The total number of people on your payroll.

Current scheme

Your present workplace pension arrangement, if you have one.

Contribution rates

What you and your staff pay in today.

Payroll frequency

Weekly, four-weekly or monthly.

Sites and languages

Whether you operate across several sites or need materials in other languages.

We host briefing sessions from Tuesday to Thursday each week across three regular time slots: 09:30, 11:30, and 14:30 UK time. Common booking formats include our Tuesday 09:30 online slot, our Wednesday 11:30 on-site slot at your workplace within forty kilometres of Bristol, and our Thursday 14:30 online slot designed to prepare materials for an upcoming board pack. Our Bristol office operates Monday to Friday from 09:00 to 17:30 UK time to manage scheduling. When you submit a briefing request, client care coordinator Priya Raman responds within two working days offering three available appointment dates.

pages.title: Who it’s for
pages.content:
WHO IT’S FOR employers 5–500

WHO IT’S
FOR

employers 5–500

Employers of 5 to 500
choosing a scheme

Our independent briefings support employers with 5 to 500 staff across the United Kingdom. We tailor our guidance to three distinct organisational groups to address their specific workplace pension challenges.

Whether you are introducing your first company pension or reviewing an arrangement made years ago, we help you prepare for provider conversations:

5–49 staff

Setting up a first scheme, meeting auto-enrolment duties and choosing straightforward default funds.

50–249 staff

Re-tendering an existing scheme, judging provider service and improving value for your workforce.

250–500 staff

Structuring pension governance across several sites, shift patterns or languages.

How do we brief employers with 5 to 49 staff setting up a first scheme?

Employers with 5 to 49 staff are typically establishing a workplace pension scheme for the very first time. In these sessions, we focus on setting up compliant contribution structures, understanding mandatory qualifying earnings thresholds, and selecting appropriate default investment funds. Small business owners and finance leads often lack dedicated in-house pension specialists, making independent guidance invaluable. We show you how minimum statutory contributions translate into monthly cash flows, how to handle payroll integration smoothly, and how to draft your first statutory communication letters. This gives early-stage companies and growing firms complete confidence before entering contracts with commercial providers.

How do we assist employers with 50 to 249 staff re-tendering an existing scheme?

Organisations with 50 to 249 staff usually have an existing pension scheme that has operated untouched for several years. We help these mid-sized employers evaluate whether their current master trust or group personal pension remains competitive and well-governed. Our briefing covers annual management charges, provider service responsiveness, member communication quality, and modern online portal usability. We review your contribution designs and identify whether salary exchange could prove beneficial. Re-tendering after five or six years ensures your organisation is not trapped in outdated fee arrangements, while providing your leadership team with clear benchmarks before inviting formal provider proposals.

How do we support employers with 250 to 500 staff across multiple sites or languages?

Employers with 250 to 500 employees frequently face complex operational hurdles, such as managing multiple regional sites, shift patterns, or multilingual workforces. For these larger organisations, our briefing examines how pension administration can remain consistent across diverse operational teams. We evaluate whether provider technology integrates cleanly with complex payroll systems and how statutory notices can be delivered effectively to workers on rotating shifts. Furthermore, we assess multi-language communication requirements, explaining how member presentations and explanatory letters in English, traditional Chinese, Japanese, French, or German can significantly improve member engagement and pension literacy across all locations.

When is our workplace briefing service not the right fit?

Kikin Advisors works exclusively with employers on corporate workplace pension scheme design, selection, and review. Our service is not suitable for individual savers seeking personal financial advice, retirement planning, wealth management, or private pension transfers. We do not sell retail investment products, recommend specific individual portfolio allocations, or manage personal assets. If you are an individual employee seeking personal retirement advice, you should consult an independent financial adviser authorised to provide individual retail guidance. Maintaining this clear operational boundary ensures our advice remains entirely focused on corporate pension governance and employer obligations.

pages.title: Pension basics
pages.content:
BASICS plain language

BASICS

plain language

How a workplace
pension works

Understanding how workplace pensions work enables employers to make informed governance and scheme choices. This guide outlines fundamental pension principles and provides plain definitions of everyday scheme terminology.

Workplace pensions in the United Kingdom operate through automatic enrolment, requiring employers to enrol eligible staff and contribute towards their retirement funds. Contributions are calculated as a percentage of qualifying earnings, shared between the employer and the employee. When staff join, their contributions are placed into a default investment fund unless they actively select alternative investment choices. Employees retain the statutory right to opt out during an initial thirty-day window after enrolment. Schemes should not be left unattended; regular re-tendering after several years ensures competitive charges and high service quality. Please note that this information provides general employer education and does not constitute individual financial advice.

What do essential contribution and investment terms mean?

Understanding core terminology simplifies scheme management.

Qualifying earnings

Qualifying earnings refers to the band of gross earnings between statutory lower and upper thresholds used to calculate minimum legal pension contributions.

Employer contribution

The employer contribution is the percentage of pay funded directly by the business, which cannot be recovered from worker wages.

Default investment fund

The default investment fund is the pre-selected investment strategy where employee contributions are automatically allocated if the member chooses not to pick specific funds.

Opt-out window

The opt-out window is the statutory one-month period following initial enrolment during which an employee may leave the scheme and receive a full refund of any deducted contributions.

What do governance and scheme structure terms mean?

Operational governance depends on several structural concepts.

Auto-enrolment

Auto-enrolment is the legal duty requiring UK employers to enrol eligible workers automatically without requiring an upfront application.

Master trust

A master trust is a multi-employer occupational pension scheme managed by an independent board of professional trustees, offering centralised compliance and investment oversight for participating businesses.

Re-tendering

Re-tendering is the formal process of reviewing and comparing alternative pension providers to ensure competitive administration charges and modern member technology.

Contribution curves

Contribution curves are graphical illustrations mapping how changing contribution levels and salary bands impact overall corporate payroll expenditures over future operating cycles.

How should employers view illustrative contribution curves versus return projections?

When examining pension plans, employers must distinguish between contribution curves and investment return projections. Kikin Advisors provides contribution curves as mathematical illustrations of cash outlay, showing how fixed contribution percentages scale across varied staff salary tiers. We never provide investment projections, return forecasts, or promises regarding future market performance. Investment markets fluctuate, and future fund values cannot be forecast or promised by any responsible adviser. Our guidance focuses strictly on cost certainty, employer statutory compliance, administrative fees, and workforce communication clarity, ensuring your leadership team bases its decisions on verifiable operational realities rather than speculative investment forecasts.

pages.content:
MEMBER SESSIONS for your staff

MEMBER
SESSIONS

for your staff

Your staff,
in their own language

We conduct focused member communication sessions to help employees understand their workplace pension without anxiety. Our sessions and translated letters ensure every team member receives clear, accessible guidance.

Our member question-and-answer session is a structured forty-five-minute presentation designed for groups of up to sixty employees. Priced at £480, these sessions can take place online or on site at your workplace. An independent adviser explains how automatic enrolment functions, what appears on monthly payslips, how employer matching contributions increase overall retirement savings, and how the default investment fund operates. We avoid industry jargon, focusing instead on answering everyday employee questions about opting out, updating personal details, and tracking accumulated funds online. This impartial format creates an open environment where staff feel comfortable asking practical questions about their benefits.

Request a briefing

Which languages are supported for member sessions and written letters?

Modern workplaces bring together diverse international teams with varied language backgrounds. To ensure equal understanding across your entire workforce, Kikin Advisors provides multilingual member support across five core languages: English, traditional Chinese, Japanese, French, and German. Advisers Inès Moreau, Jonas Weber, and Mei-Lin Chou lead sessions tailored for French, German, and Mandarin-speaking personnel. In addition to spoken sessions, we translate member explanatory letters into second languages for £180 per language. Providing statutory notices and scheme overviews in a worker native tongue dramatically increases engagement, builds trust in corporate benefits, and ensures compliance across international organisations.

Who leads our advisory and technical contribution design?

Our advisory team is led by founder Ruth Halloran, who established Kikin Advisors in 2014 and has conducted employer briefings for over a decade. Working alongside her is senior adviser Kwame Asante, who specialises in contribution design, salary exchange modelling, and complex payroll structuring for organisations of up to 500 staff. Scheme analyst Daniel Ortega authors our provider comparison notes, evaluating master trust governance, administrative capabilities, and fee competitiveness across up to three shortlisted providers. Together, they combine deep regulatory understanding with practical commercial insight, giving leadership teams rigorous, objective analysis before any long-term pension contracts are signed.

Who oversees multilingual member communications and client care?

Effective communication across diverse workforces is supported by our dedicated language specialists. Inès Moreau serves as our adviser for French-speaking employers and cross-border teams. Jonas Weber provides specialist advisory support for German-speaking organisations operating in the UK. Mei-Lin Chou coordinates member communications, delivering staff presentations and written guidance in both English and Mandarin. Scheduling and ongoing client care are managed by Priya Raman, who coordinates initial briefing requests, distributes pre-briefing documentation, and ensures written summaries arrive punctually within five working days. This multidisciplinary team ensures every employer receives responsive, culturally fluent support from their initial enquiry onward.

INDE-
PENDENT

Why do we operate exclusively on a fee-only basis without commission?

Complete independence is the cornerstone of our practice. Kikin Advisors takes absolutely no commission, marketing allowances, or introducer fees from pension providers, master trusts, or life companies. We are paid solely by the transparent fees agreed with our employer clients. Because we do not sell financial products, our advisers have no commercial incentive to steer you toward any particular provider. We never promise investment returns or speculative future outcomes; our contribution curves serve strictly as mathematical illustrations of cost structures. This fee-only commitment ensures that every recommendation and observation is made solely in the best interests of your business and employees.

pages.content:
STORIES three employers

Read how employers with 5 to 500 staff used our sixty-minute briefing to review and select workplace pensions. These case studies describe qualitative outcomes from real engagements without artificial claims or inflated figures.

“We finally understood our pension duties”

Halden Bakery set up a first workplace pension across six shops. Ruth Halloran walked the managers through contribution duties and default funds, leaving an easy routine for shop staff.

After six years with the same provider, Venn & Ashworth compared the alternatives. Kwame Asante and Daniel Ortega set out governance and charges so the partners could choose with confidence.

How did Halden Bakery navigate establishing their first workplace pension?

Halden Bakery operates six retail bakery shops with a total of 48 staff across their regional operations. When preparing their first workplace pension scheme, the founder wanted clear visibility over ongoing operational costs without getting bogged down in complex industry jargon. Principal adviser Ruth Halloran led a sixty-minute employer briefing with the bakery owners. She walked them through qualifying earnings calculations, explained how employer contributions integrate with monthly payroll, and mapped out simple contribution curves. The owners gained total clarity regarding their statutory obligations, selected an appropriate default scheme, and successfully communicated the new pension arrangement to their shop floor staff.

How did Venn & Ashworth Architects approach re-tendering after six years?

Venn & Ashworth Architects employs 31 professional staff and had remained with their initial pension provider for six consecutive years without a formal review. Senior adviser Kwame Asante and scheme analyst Daniel Ortega conducted a sixty-minute briefing with the practice directors to examine how the market had progressed. Daniel authored a provider comparison note examining three alternative master trusts, highlighting differences in member platform usability and governance oversight. The practice used these objective insights to re-tender their scheme effectively, modernising their employee benefit offering and establishing an updated contribution structure that received enthusiastic approval from their architectural team.

How did Northway Logistics brief a shift-based multilingual workforce?

Northway Logistics operates an Avonmouth depot employing 220 staff working across three rotating shifts. The company needed to update its pension communications to engage a diverse workforce with varying language backgrounds. Member communications specialist Mei-Lin Chou organised dedicated staff sessions in English and Mandarin, matching the primary languages of the depot workers. By holding forty-five-minute Q&A meetings tailored to shift schedules and distributing translated explanatory letters, the depot achieved outstanding attendance and comprehension. Management praised the calm, inclusive approach, noting that employees across all shifts felt genuinely informed about their pension contributions and employer matching benefits.

ABOUT & OFFICE since 2014

Kikin Advisors was established in 2014 by Ruth Halloran to provide impartial workplace pension briefings for UK employers. We operate from our central Bristol office, offering independent guidance free from provider commission.

ABOUT

since 2014

Founded 2014
in Bristol

How has Kikin Advisors developed since its founding in 2014?

Ruth Halloran founded Kikin Advisors in 2014 after recognising that UK employers faced significant confusion when navigating mandatory workplace pension regulations. Most available guidance came directly from commercial providers seeking to sell proprietary schemes or commission-driven intermediaries. Ruth established Kikin Advisors on a strictly fee-only advisory model, ensuring employers could access objective, independent guidance before committing to long-term contracts. Over the past decade, our practice has grown to a seven-person specialist team supporting employers of 5 to 500 staff. While our technical capabilities and language coverage have expanded, our founding principle remains unchanged: helping employers understand their options before they sign.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
PRIVACY plain words

This privacy policy details how Kikin Advisors collects, processes, and protects organisational and personal information. We maintain rigorous confidentiality standards in compliance with United Kingdom data protection regulations.

What information does Kikin Advisors collect from employer clients?

We collect only the information necessary to arrange and conduct workplace pension briefings and related documentation services. This includes organisational contact information such as employer names, business addresses, telephone numbers, and designated staff contact email addresses. In addition, when preparing for your briefing, we collect operational data through our ten-question pre-briefing questionnaire, including total staff headcounts, general salary distributions, existing pension provider names, and current contribution structures. We do not collect individual employee personal financial records, national insurance numbers, or personal banking information, as our advisory services are delivered exclusively at the corporate employer level.

How do we process, store, and protect your organisational data?

All data collected is used solely to evaluate your workplace pension requirements, conduct your sixty-minute briefing, generate your five-day written summary, and issue commercial invoices. We maintain strict digital and physical security protocols at our registered office on the 3rd floor, 27 Wharf Lane, Bristol BS1 6QX, United Kingdom. Because we operate entirely independently on a fee-only basis, we never sell, rent, or share your data with commercial pension providers, financial marketing networks, or external third parties. Client records are retained only for as long as required by UK corporate accounting and professional regulatory record-keeping standards.

What data rights do you possess and how can you contact us?

Under United Kingdom data protection law, you have the right to request access to any personal data we hold concerning your organisation, request corrections to inaccurate records, or request the deletion of your information where retention is no longer legally mandated. If you subscribe to our briefing slot notification list, you can withdraw your consent and unsubscribe at any time. For all data protection enquiries, subject access requests, or privacy concerns, please contact our data administrator by emailing briefings@kikin-advisors.example or writing to our Bristol office. We respond promptly to all data enquiries within standard statutory timeframes.

pages.title: Terms

posts.title: What to Evaluate Before Choosing or Re-Tendering a Workplace Pension Scheme
posts.excerpt: An independent sixty-minute briefing gives employers the structural clarity needed to evaluate workplace pension schemes before signing contracts with commercial providers.
posts.content:
Choosing a workplace pension scheme is one of the most consequential financial and operational decisions an employer makes. For organisations employing between 5 and 500 staff, automatic enrolment obligations require ongoing contributions, accurate payroll calculations, and clear statutory communications. Yet all too often, employers enter negotiations with commercial pension providers or master trusts without a clear, objective framework. Commercial sales representatives naturally emphasise their own investment platforms and proprietary administrative tools. Without independent analysis, company directors and finance leaders risk locking their business into unsuitable contribution structures, uncompetitive annual management charges, or communication formats that confuse staff.

Taking one hour to examine your scheme before signing any contract changes the entire dynamic.

Ruth Halloran, founder

Founded in 2014 by Ruth Halloran in Bristol, Kikin Advisors was established on a simple premise: employers deserve impartial guidance before they commit. Our sixty-minute employer briefing breaks down the decision into three manageable twenty-minute stages. In the first twenty minutes, an independent adviser walks you through how your plan is assembled, examining contribution designs, qualifying earnings calculations, and default investment funds. Seeing your contribution curves drawn out clearly on a whiteboard illustrates how costs scale across salary tiers, providing transparent cost illustrations rather than speculative investment projections.

The middle twenty minutes shift focus to your workforce. A workplace pension only succeeds if employees understand the value of what their employer contributes. We review how statutory communications can be conveyed in plain language, eliminating bureaucratic jargon. For companies with diverse workforces, multi-site operations, or shift-based teams, member communications must bridge cultural and language divides. Whether through forty-five-minute staff question-and-answer sessions or explanatory letters in English, traditional Chinese, Japanese, French, or German, clear communication reduces employee anxiety, limits administrative enquiries, and prevents unnecessary opt-outs.

The final twenty minutes determine your single next conversation. Rather than leaving you with administrative confusion, we identify the exact discussion your organisation needs next. We equip your team with twelve critical questions to ask prospective providers, allowing you to compare administration charges, online portal usability, and governance standards across competing master trusts. Following the briefing, we provide a concise written summary and contribution-curve sheet within five working days, giving your board of directors the objective evidence needed to proceed with confidence.

Because Kikin Advisors operates strictly on a fee-only basis, charging a flat £390 fee for the sixty-minute briefing with summary included, we accept absolutely no commission from any pension provider. We never promise investment returns or market outcomes. Whether you are setting up a first scheme for 48 staff or re-tendering an existing arrangement after six years, independent preparation ensures you choose a workplace pension that serves your business and your people effectively.

Written by Ruth Halloran, principal adviser at Kikin Advisors. This note is general information for employers, not personal advice.
